image_description: A side-profile view of a large bison standing in a grassy field. The animal features a massive, shaggy dark brown forequarter with a prominent shoulder hump, transitioning to lighter brown, less dense fur on the hindquarters. It has a large head with a visible short curved horn, a beard, and sturdy legs partially obscured by tall grass.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible in profile, showing a broad structure and at least one distinct, short, curved horn consistent with bison anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct mass of long, dark hair hangs from the chin and throat area, matching the description of a bison beard.
The eye is visible as a dark spot within the heavy fur of the face.
No large, protruding ears are visible; the ear region is covered by the thick mane/fur, consistent with the 'hidden' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The animal exhibits a massive build with a high shoulder line (withers) that slopes down towards the rear, characteristic of bison proportions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a clear textural and color distinction between the dark, shaggy forequarters and the smoother hindquarters, with a pronounced hump at the shoulders.
The fur on the rear half of the body is visibly shorter, smoother, and lighter in color compared to the front.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible horn is relatively small in proportion to the massive head and body.
The lower legs and feet are completely occluded by the tall green grass and white foreground flowers/debris. Hooves cannot be verified.
The rear of the bison is cut off by the right edge of the image frame; the tail is not visible.

The joint area of the front leg seems to lack clear anatomical definition, appearing somewhat fused or indistinct where it meets the upper leg and chest fur.
